shortName: University of Alabama at Birmingham Marnix E. Heersink School of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: UAB is committed to recruiting and retaining outstanding students, faculty and staff from all backgrounds, providing open and equal access to resources and opportunities, and equipping all campus community members for success.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The Associate Dean for Students  may approve a voluntary or involuntary leave of absence for medical students in cases of severe extenuating circumstances (medical reasons, financial reasons, personal reasons, etc.). In cases where these circumstances exist, the Associate Dean for Students may approve a withdrawal from a course, all courses, or from the School of Medicine. Students may be placed on Involuntary Leave of Absence for academic or administrative reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The student-run organizations center around varied affiliations and interests. Many members use these activities to enjoy the camaraderie of fellow students, explore specialty fields, become involved in advocacy, and serve the community. Students are also assigned to Learning Communities. In addition to forming the basic unit for class, lab small groups, and student government, these communities offer opportunities for social interaction, peer support, and professional development.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
UAB is a four-campus medical school, with Birmingham serving as the main campus and regional campuses in Huntsville, Montgomery, and Tuscaloosa. Students spend the first two years of medical school in Birmingham and are assigned to one of the campuses for their clinical years.

The Birmingham campus is part of the UAB Medical Center, a world-renowned academic medical center with more than 70 research centers across 82 city blocks.

The Huntsville Regional Medical Campus primary teaching hospital is the Huntsville Hospital, which is the second-largest in Alabama.  

Montgomery Regional Medical Campus primary teaching hospital is Baptist Medical Center South and has opportunities for courses with Montgomery AIDS Outreach, Montgomery Medical Outreach Ministries, and the Alabama Department of Public Health.

 Tuscaloosa Regional Campus is located on the campus of The University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa. Students participate in the Tuscaloosa Longitudinal Integrated Curriculum (LIC).
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Limited housing is available on campus. Most medical students live off-campus and find affordable housing within a 3-15-minute commute to the campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: "Ensuring Access: How DSS and MSS Empower UAB Heersink School of Medicine Students to Thrive": https://www.uab.edu/medicine/news/medical-education/ensuring-access-how-dss-and-mss-empower-uab-heersink-school-of-medicine-students-to-thrive
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: UAB Heersink School of Medicine has a friendly and close-knit community. Our energetic atmosphere makes it easy for students to connect and support each other. Our campus culture strongly emphasizes health and well-being, providing plenty of resources to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to feel their best as they tackle any challenges that come their way throughout their medical careers.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: During the first two years of medical school, students who choose to live within walking distance of the school may be able to do so without a vehicle.  A vehicle is a necessity during clinical coursework.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Academic Success Office within Medical Student Services offers academic advising, learning style assessment, study skills development, and academic consultation for individuals and in groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Within the first two weeks of Medical School.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Our active learning approach to education includes Small Groups, Team Based Learning, Labs, and some lectures.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical Rotations begin at the end of the 2nd year and include Internal Medicine, Surgery, Pediatrics, OBGYN, Neurology, Psychiatry and Family Medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at most lectures is optional.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The four-year program emphasizes the fundamentals underlying clinical medical practice, with attention to the emotional, cultural, and social characteristics of patients and to the importance of adapting care to meet their needs. The Preclinical curriculum integrates basic and clinical sciences into organ system modules co-directed by basic scientists and clinicians. The objective of the curriculum is for students to learn basic sciences in a clinically relevant context, teaching them to think comprehensively about organ function and disease rather than to memorize mountains of facts.  The first two years also provide training in medical professionalism, interviewing, and physical examination. The third and fourth years consist of required rotations and electives, with clinical experiences in both hospital and ambulatory settings. There are structured opportunities for research.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
Over six decades, the University of Alabama at Birmingham School of Medicine has emerged as a national leader in primary care medical education, in pioneering research that improves people's lives, and in providing humanistic patient care at the bedside.  

In addition, the Primary Care Track has been established as an option for students that are interested in pursing Primary Care. Participants that participate in this program are assigned to the Tuscaloosa Regional Campus their 3rd year in medical school and part of their 4th year.  For more information visit:  https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/education/md-program/primary-care-track
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: UAB medical students have a number of options for engaging in research while pursuing their medical education. These options range from summer research experiences to dual degree programs. Each year students present their research at  the Dale J. Benos Medical Student Research Day. Short term research opportunities are available for medical students who choose to undertake research during the summer between the first and second years of medical school. Opportunities exist for students to participate in basic biomedical, clinical, translational, and public health research. For long term research opportunities medical students who have completed their preclinical years may opt to take a year out to engage in elective research. Students may choose to stay at UAB or go to another institution for their research. There are a number of competitive fellowships available to support this form of research. All medical students are required to engage in a mentored scholarly project.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service Learning Opportunities are available for students. Equal Access Birmingham (student run clinic) is one example. http://www.uab.edu/medicine/servicelearning/
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText:
All medical students complete a longitudinal Scholarly Activity project. 
 https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/current-students/scholarly-activity
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: UAB Hospital, Children's of Alabama,  Birmingham Veteran's Administration Hospital and Callahan Eye Hospital, Huntsville Hospital, Baptist Medical Center South, and DCH Regional Medical Center.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pre-clinical grades are pass and fail. Clinical grades are honors, high pass, pass and fail. http://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/current-students/policies-procedures

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine was founded in Mobile in 1859 and has been located in Birmingham since 1945. There are 4 regional campuses: Birmingham, Huntsville, Montgomery and Tuscaloosa.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
UAB Heersink Mission and Vision Statements
Mission
To advance health and healing through patient care, education, and discovery.

Vision
To be a leader in making a global impact through innovative care, transformative discovery, and collaborative teaching and learning.

Admissions Statement
The UAB Heersink School of Medicine selects applicants poised to become exceptional clinicians, physician-scientists, and medical educators. We seek academically qualified candidates from all backgrounds and experiences who exhibit strong competence in one or more of the following: dedication to serving others, cultural sensitivity, communication skills, teamwork, and leadership.  Our holistic admissions process values applicants with a demonstrated interest in serving underserved rural and urban communities, addressing medical disparities, advancing research and innovation, and/or practicing primary care medicine. We are committed to recruiting and training applicants from Alabama, students with close ties to Alabama, and/or students who demonstrate a passion for the mission of the UAB Heersink School of Medicine.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The UAB Early Medical School Acceptance Program (EMSAP) is designed to give exceptional high school graduates an opportunity to take advantage of the best resources of the undergraduate and medical programs through a mentored relationship with faculty. This is not an accelerated program, rather a program to allow gifted students to explore a broad range of educational, research and community service opportunities beyond the typical Premedical experiences.

Students are selected in their senior year of high school. Preference is given to Alabama residents and applicants from out of state with close ties to the state of Alabama. Read Less

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: We ask for a response (not a commitment) within two weeks prior to April 30 and one week after April 30.  Plan to enroll date is April 30 and Commit to enroll date is 28 days prior to class start.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Students from schools without a committee letter can fulfill our letter requirement with the following:

Letter Packet
A packet or set of letters is assembled and distributed by your institution, often by the institution’s career center. A letter packet may include a cover sheet from your pre-health committee or advisor; however, in contrast to a committee letter, a letter packet does not include an evaluative letter from your pre-health committee or advisor.

Three Individual Letters
Individual letters should include at least one letter from a faculty member (preferably a science faculty member) and two letters from other faculty or individuals who can provide in-depth evaluation and recommendation.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Committee Letter - Preferred Option
A committee letter is authored by a pre-health committee or pre-health advisor and intended to represent your institution's evaluation of you. A committee letter may or may not include additional letters written in support of your application. If you have committee letters from two different programs/schools, list one as your committee letter and include the other as an individual letter.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Virtual interviews include a one-on-one with a member of the admissions committee and a nine-station MMI.  Interviewees also hear from the admissions team and meet with current medical students during the virtual interview day program.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Virtual interviews include a one-on-one with a member of the admissions committee and a nine-station MMI.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Recorded video interviews are not available.

medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: We recommend applicants submit within two weeks of receiving a secondary invitation or by November 15, at the latest.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We will use the most recent MCAT total score for consideration for secondary invitations. The committee will consider the applicants’ scores from all MCAT tests when evaluating applicants for interview and admission.  Particular attention is paid to the Biological and Biochemical Foundations of Living Systems and the Chemical and Physical Foundations of Biological Systems sections.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo:
Applicants with a 495 total MCAT score are typically eligible to receive an invitation to complete our secondary application.  The EMSAP program has different MCAT criteria.

See website for more information: https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/selection-criteria
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo:
Alabama residents must have a 3.0 science (BCPM) GPA at the undergraduate level or a 3.0 science (BCPM) GPA after 20 or more BCPM credits at the post-baccalaureate or graduate level to receive the secondary application invitation. Since pass/fail grades are not included in the GPA, they do not count toward the 20 credit requirement at the post-baccalaureate and graduate level to receive the secondary application.

Out-of-state applicants must have a 3.3 science (BCPM) GPA at the undergraduate level or a 3.3 science (BCPM) GPA after 20 or more BCPM credits at the post baccalaureate or graduate level to receive an invitation to complete the secondary application. Since pass/fail grades are not included in the GPA, they do not count toward the 20 credit requirement at the post-baccalaureate and graduate level to receive the secondary application.

See website for more information: https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/selection-criteria

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept courses taken at the community college.  Committee will assess performance in these courses as well as courses taken at the university level to determine readiness for medical education.  Students are encouraged to take rigorous prerequisite courses to build a solid foundation.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants have the ability to upload any significant updates to their application files through the application portal system.  Only updates that are received before committee review will be considered for decisions.  After the committee reviews the application, the committee does not re-review applications based on updates submitted.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: UAB offers a comprehensive advising program to aid students with budgeting, debt management, and financial aid.   Through the generosity of donors, we offer nearly $6 million dollars annually to medical students. State residents committed to rural practice in Alabama may qualify for additional aid.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The general tuition and fees for students attending the University of Alabama School of Medicine are payable in two installments. The first payment is due on or before September 1 and the second and final installment is due on or before January 1.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Master of Science in Biomedical and Health Sciences
The MS in Biomedical and Health Sciences (MSBHS) Program is an 11-month program designed to provide coursework and experiences to help students transition from undergrad to medical, dental, optometry, physician assistant, and other health professional programs. 
https://www.uab.edu/shp/cds/biomedical-and-health-sciences

Other Pathway Programs:

Blaze to MD
This program is an 11-month pathway designed for students who have the potential to succeed in medicine and need more academic preparation in basic sciences. Students accepted to the Blaze to MD program complete the Master of Science in Biomedical and Health Sciences program before starting medical school.
https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/education/md-program/blaze-to-md-program

Rural Medicine
UAB has two rural medicine pre-matriculation programs to help students prepare for careers in rural medicine.
https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/education/md-program/rural-medicine

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: In early April, a two-tier waitlist is created and applicants are notified of their tier placement.   # of waitlist offers over the last 3 years: 2023 = 14; 2024 = 17; 2025 = 0

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Online and community college courses are accepted unless otherwise noted.  We prefer labs to be in person.  Students must receive a “C” or better in required courses.  For information about required courses and competencies, please visit our Selection Criteria page here: https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/selection-criteria
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Prerequisite courses do not have a date requirement.  Applicants should have completed most prereqs before applying to medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
UAB Heersink uses a comprehensive, merit-based, and mission-driven admissions process to select applicants poised to become exceptional clinicians, physician scientists and medical educators.  Competitive applicants are those who are academically prepared to handle the rigors of medical education with strong competency in communication skills, teamwork, leadership, and service to others.

Our mission-based approach values applicants who contribute to one or more of our mission areas including academic medicine/research, community service, intent to serve Alabama communities, and primary care.

We are committed to recruiting and training applicants from Alabama, applicants from out of state with close ties to Alabama, and/or applicants from out of state who demonstrate passion for the mission of the UAB Heersink School of Medicine.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Exposure to medicine and physicians is a requirement for consideration.  Medically related experiences (work, volunteer, or shadowing) are expected in order to observe the patient/physician relationship and confirm an interest in medicine.
